items.summary: Pfizer has decided to join the in vivo CAR-T race, penning a $2.6 billion deal for three preclinical candidates from China’s Starna Therapeutics.

items.title: At Fierce’s London event, Big Pharmas tell biotechs to ‘be transparent’ to secure deals
items.summary: Every biotech looking for a suitor wants to know: What does it take to charm a Big Pharma into a deal?

items.title: Vertex signs $220M deal with Genomics to re-up long-running discovery pact
items.summary: Vertex Pharmaceuticals has re-upped its ties with sequencing specialist Genomics in a deal worth up to $220 million, signing on for an extra four years on top of the eight the companies have already worked together.

items.title: Priavoid’s Alzheimer’s pill fails to prove efficacy in phase 2 trial
items.summary: Priavoid’s pill for Alzheimer's disease has failed to prove its effectiveness in a phase 2 dementia study, although the German biotech pointed to encouraging signs in the longer-term data.

items.title: FDA clears MiniMed Fit tubeless insulin pump
items.summary: MiniMed announced has picked up FDA clearance of its tubeless insulin pump, the MiniMed Fit.

items.title: Cognito phase 3 flops in light-and-sound Alzheimer's trial, but sees ‘signal’ for HOPE
items.summary: Cognito Therapeutics said its phase 3 HOPE study of Spectris AD, an investigational, non-invasive, at-home Alzheimer's therapy that uses light and sound stimulation to engage brain activity, failed to meet its primary endpoint.

items.title: Merck axes $2.7B BTK inhibitor program after seeing phase 3 data
items.summary: Merck & Co. has stopped a trio of phase 3 blood cancer trials after one study suggested the benefits of the BTK inhibitor may fail to outweigh the risks, bringing the curtain down on a program stemming from a $2.7 billion takeover.

items.title: Heidi Overton’s FDA nomination pulled by White House
items.summary: The White House is pulling Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead the FDA just hours before the Senate was scheduled to vote on her confirmation.

items.title: FDA’s complete response letter for Summit’s ivonescimab cites China-heavy data beyond survival miss
items.summary: The FDA’s rejection of Summit Therapeutics’ closely watched PD-1xVEGF bispecific ivonescimab extends beyond its previously reported failure to show a statistically significant overall survival benefit.

items.title: Scientists uncover ‘very detailed map’ of an enzyme target for rare metabolic disease
items.summary: For some rare genetic diseases, the problem isn't a missing protein but the buildup of toxic molecules that the body can no longer clear away.

items.title: Medtronic pays $380M-plus for Contego Medical buyout
items.summary: Medtronic is boosting its cardiovascular disease portfolio with a deal to buy up carotid artery disease and peripheral thrombectomy tech company Contego Medical.

items.title: Kyntra axes mid-stage ADC, adding to years of stumbles
items.summary: Beleaguered Kyntra Bio can’t catch a break. Formerly known as FibroGen, the company has endured a series of woes over the last few years, and now the biotech is cutting a clinical antibody-drug conjugate program from its mid-stage lineup.

items.title: Why 2027 could be ‘Europe’s year to shine’: Panelists debate biotech funding at Fierce’s London event
items.summary: Panelists at Fierce Biotech's London Life Sciences Week event discussed whether Europe can pull its weight in biopharma investment next year against the gravitational pull of the U.S. and China.

items.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5B series C months after $2.1B round
items.summary: Isomorphic Labs has raised a $5 billion series C round, marking the second time in six months that the AI drug development startup has pulled off a multibillion-dollar financing.

items.title: AriBio’s oral Alzheimer’s drug meets monotherapy goal in phase 3 as Fosun weighs licensing option
items.summary: AriBio’s erectile dysfunction med-turned Alzheimer’s disease candidate mirodenafil has delivered some mixed results from a global phase 3 trial. Fosun Pharma has an option to in-license the PDE5 inhibitor.

items.title: Marrow extracts $120M series B to advance preclinical blood disease therapy
items.summary: A new biotech targeting blood disorders, aptly called Marrow Therapeutics, has launched with $173 million in combined funding and a preclinical lead program aimed at sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia.

items.title: Sellas marks 9-month survival benefit in late-stage leukemia vaccine study
items.summary: Sellas Life Sciences’ cancer vaccine for acute myeloid leukemia has passed a phase 3 test with a more than nine-month improvement in overall survival.

items.title: Lilly signs $5.9B deal with Stipple to unlock oncology targets
items.summary: Eli Lilly has struck a $5.9 billion deal to partner with Stipple Bio on oncology drug candidates that more precisely target tumor cells.

items.title: CDMO Lotte inks commercial production deal as work on South Korean plant wraps
items.summary: Lotte Biologics, which was established in 2022, inked a major manufacturing deal with an unnamed pharmaceutical company as the South Korean CDMO gears up for commercial production at its new multi-billion-dollar Songdo Bio Campus near Seoul.

items.title: AI’s Real Prize: Building Tomorrow’s CI Capability
items.summary: AI is becoming a commodity. Javier Vega explains why the next advantage in competitive intelligence comes from people, judgment and scale.

items.title: BMS' ph. 3 Alzheimer's psychosis teaser builds confidence in Cobenfy expansion plan
items.summary: After delaying the phase 3 readout of its Alzheimer’s psychosis program for Cobenfy earlier this year, Bristol Myers Squibb is offering an early peek that appears to bode well for the high-stakes data drops ahead, even as the fine details remain hazy.

items.title: Beren clinches long-awaited FDA nod for cyclodextrin drug in Niemann-Pick disease
items.summary: Beren Therapeutic's Lembaz was cleared by the FDA to treat the neurogenerative disorder Niemann-Pick disease type C in children as small as 15 pounds. It's the first NPC treatment to improve survival and to treat the cholesterol transport dysfunction that drives the disease.

items.title: FDA moves to yank Salerno's liquid cholesterol drug approval on missing reports
items.summary: In a notice posted on the Federal Register Wednesday, the FDA said that it has proposed withdrawing the approval for Salerno’s FloLipid, an oral suspension formulation of the long-approved cholesterol lowering medication simvastatin.

items.title: Novo expands DTC program Novocare to support Wegovy users through holistic health journey
items.summary: Members who sign up for Novo's new Novocare can benefit from holistic health services meant to support Wegovy users throughout the entirety of their weight loss journey.

items.title: Cosentyx bags FDA nod for 11th indication as Novartis looks to buffer 2029 patent cliff
items.summary: Cosentyx's latest FDA approval marks the aging biologic's 11th indication and the first of the anti-IL-17 class to be approved for polymyalgia rheumatica.

items.title: GSK scores FDA approval for Nelkarmi, its 2nd lung cancer drug from Nuvalent deal
items.summary: On a hot streak, GSK has won a third high-profile FDA approval in recent weeks, this time for the second lung cancer drug from the British pharma’s $10.6 billion acquisition of Nuvalent earlier this year.

items.title: AZ defeats health plan lawsuit alleging Soliris antitrust maneuvers
items.summary: Winning a ruling in their favor Monday, AstraZeneca and its rare disease unit Alexion have successfully sidestepped U.S. antitrust allegations linked to aging rare disease drug Soliris.

items.title: Viatris takes the wheel as Cadillac F1 team's new global pharma partner
items.summary: The multi-year partnership with Cadillac's Formula 1 Team makes Viatris the latest pharma to rev up a marketing play in the auto racing zone.

items.title: Roche’s next major breast cancer drug, Wilserdly, secures FDA approval as 4th oral SERD
items.summary: Roche’s giredestrant took the first step toward what some analysts project could exceed $10 billion in peak annual sales, winning FDA approval for certain patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.

items.title: BeOne commits $3M to expand CLL Society patient education partnership
items.summary: BeOne Medicines has expanded its partnership with CLL Society, entering into a three-year, $3 million pact to support leukemia and lymphoma patients.

items.title: USV chided by FDA over contamination risks at India site
items.summary: Indian drug manufacturer USV was hit with a warning letter from the FDA that outlined three major violations. The observations largely centered on a lack of procedures that could lead to microbial and particulate contamination.

items.title: Regulatory tracker: Teva lands new FDA nod 3 weeks after picking up Igalmi
items.summary: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.title: Leo Pharma IPO plans stalled by market volatility: Bloomberg
items.summary: Ownership behind Danish dermatology drugmaker Leo Pharma has opted to delay the company's plans for a 2026 IPO in the wake of ongoing market volatility.

items.title: Roche’s Gazyva adds 3rd immune indication with first FDA nod for primary membranous nephropathy
items.summary: As Roche’s Gazyva comes under pressure in blood cancer, the anti-CD20 antibody keeps expanding its reach in autoimmune diseases.

items.title: Eisai, Linus Health launch ‘brain health’ digital resource
items.summary: Japanese Big Pharma Eisai is teaming up with Boston-based digital health company Linus Health to create new “Brain Health Reports.”

items.title: With Klygefa approvals, AZ expands myasthenia gravis domain beyond Soliris, Ultomiris
items.summary: Continuing to harvest a bounty of autumn approvals, AstraZeneca has picked up nods for its C5 inhibitor gefurulimab to treat generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) on both sides of the Atlantic.

items.title: Quality over quantity: Healthcare messages not tuned into patient needs, survey finds
items.summary: 58% of patients out of a 1,500 patient survey reported that healthcare communications don't consistently feel relevant to their needs, behavioral science-focused Lirio found.

items.title: Digital Twins: Advancing Clinical Evidence Strategy
items.summary: Learn how patient digital twins can model treatment scenarios, strengthen comparator strategies and support evidence generation.

items.title: Measurement Everywhere: Why the Future Can’t Be Measured in the Rearview Mirror
items.summary: Stop measuring marketing in the rearview mirror. See how continuous measurement turns trusted signals into smarter decisions and action.
